page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core using multithreading. The system includes 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set capabilities include standard AVX, cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, along with bit manipulation extensions. The configuration does not include discrete GPUs or local attached storage.

Benchmark analysis shows strong single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, placing in the top 25% of evaluated machines. Multi-core performance, overall Geekbench score, and Passmark CPU rating fall within the middle average range. Memory bandwidth measures 1013.33 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 93.7 GB/sec for uncached 256MB blocks. Small-model LLM text generation demonstrates strong throughput at 277.2 tokens per second for 135M parameter models. The instance achieves 14.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.61 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Offering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides steady compute density suitable for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external persistent disks for stateful applications, while missing AVX-512 instructions limits specialized vector computing workloads. Dedicated CPU allocation and consistent single-thread execution ensure predictable cost efficiency for general compute scenarios.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by a 16 vCPU AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 8 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading and 64 GB of memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware capabilities include hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptography along with standard AVX extensions. The instance lacks attached local storage and dedicated GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the n2d-standard-16 exhibits strong single-core CPU execution and efficient small-model text generation speed, alongside middle-tier results across multi-core Passmark, Geekbench, Redis operation rates, and memory bandwidth tests. With dedicated CPU allocation and standard resource ratios, this instance provides steady compute efficiency for web application serving, software compilation, database workloads, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
